definition_en: to feel envious about something another person has or achieves; to give something reluctantly
core_image: 嘴上说着恭喜，眼睛却一直黏在对方的新车上
scene: 他嘴上道贺，眼睛却一直盯着对方的新车。He congratulated her, but he clearly begrudged her the new car.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：begrudge 指嫉妒别人所得；句意是他嘴上道贺，却显然眼红她的新车。

senses.title: To envy what another has
senses.definition: to feel annoyed or envious because someone else has something you want
senses.definitionCN: 因别人拥有你想要的东西而心生不快或嫉妒
senses.example: No one begrudged him the prize; he had earned it.
senses.exampleCN: 没人眼红他得奖，那是他应得的。
senses.why: The noun grudge is a secret resentment, and be- turns it into actively holding that resentment against someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词 grudge 是暗暗的怨恨，前缀 be- 使它变成「把怨恨加在某人身上」。

senses.title: To give unwillingly
senses.definition: to give or allow something only with reluctance
senses.definitionCN: 只在极不情愿的情况下给予或允许
senses.example: She begrudged every hour spent on paperwork.
senses.exampleCN: 她在文书上花掉的每一小时都让她肉痛。
senses.why: If you resent another having something, giving it away feels like a loss, so the envy sense slides into reluctance.
senses.whyCN: 既然别人拥有会让你不快，那么把东西给出去就像是一种损失，于是「嫉妒」滑向「不情愿」。

intro.en: Begrudge is be- plus grudge, and grudge began as a sound: the low murmur of complaint heard behind someone back.
intro.cn: begrudge 是 be- 加 grudge，而 grudge 起初是一个声音：有人在背后低声嘟囔的那种抱怨。

items.en: A Germanic root meant to grumble, the sound of low complaint.
items.cn: 一个日耳曼语词根意为低声抱怨，即小声嘟囔之声。

items.en: Old French grouchier means to murmur and to grumble, the source of grudge.
items.cn: 古法语 grouchier 意为嘟囔、抱怨，是 grudge 的来源。

items.en: Middle English grudge names a secret resentment held against someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 grudge 指对某人暗藏的怨恨。

items.en: The covering prefix be- turns the noun into a verb of holding the grudge.
items.cn: 「遍覆」前缀 be- 把名词变成「怀着怨恨」的动词。

items.en: The verb widens from envy to giving something unwillingly.
items.cn: 该动词由「嫉妒」扩为「不情愿地给予」。

items.en: The commonest pattern is to begrudge someone something they have.
items.cn: 最常见搭配是 begrudge someone something。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps other be- verbs so the prefix pattern stays visible; the near-meaning group runs from the plain feeling to the act of giving sparingly.
note.cn: 形近组保留其他 be- 动词，让前缀规律一直可见；近义组由朴素的情感一路走到「给得吝啬」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：be-「加上」+ grudge「怨恨」= begrudge 把怨恨加到别人头上，即嫉妒别人所得；进而表示「不情愿地给」。名词 grudge、形容词 grudging 同族。

root: 由前缀 be- 加 grudge 构成；grudge 出自古法语 grouchier「嘟囔、抱怨」，深层为日耳曼语「低声抱怨」的拟声词根，约 1400 年进入中古英语指暗藏的怨恨。begrudge 同世纪出现，17 世纪扩出「不情愿给予」义。

abstract.en: See a light kept on through the night.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏整夜不灭的灯。

abstract.en: See hands folded in quiet prayer.

examples.en: Her belief in herself never faded.

definition_zh: 相信；认为；信仰
definition_en: to think that something is true, or to have faith in someone
core_image: 听完解释后点头表示相信
scene: 听完对方的解释，她慢慢点了点头。I believe his story.
sceneCN: 这里 believe 是「相信」（第 1 个义项：认为某话为真）；句意是我相信他讲的事。

derivatives.zh: believe 的名词形式，义为「信念」
由 believe 加 -able 构成，义为「可信的」

senses.title: To accept as true
senses.definition: to accept that something is true
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事是真的
senses.example: I believe his story.
senses.exampleCN: 我相信他讲的事。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the mind says yes to a claim.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：心里对一种说法说「是」。

senses.title: To think or suppose
senses.definition: to think that something is probably the case
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事很可能是这样
senses.example: I believe she is still in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 我想她还在办公室。
senses.why: In everyday speech belief softens into a polite opinion.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，「相信」弱化为一种客气的看法。

senses.title: To have faith in
senses.definition: to trust in someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物怀有信心
senses.example: She believes in the power of kindness.
senses.exampleCN: 她相信善意的力量。
senses.why: With in added, the word moves from facts to values.
senses.whyCN: 加上 in 之后，词义从事实转向价值。

intro.en: Believe is be- plus an old word for dear, meaning to hold dear.

normal.en: The noun is belief, spelled with f.
normal.cn: 名词是带 f 的 belief。

normal.en: Believe in means trust or have faith.
normal.cn: believe in 指信任或信仰。

normal.en: The past tense is believed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 believed。

normal.en: I believe softens a plain opinion.
normal.cn: I believe 能让看法说得更客气。

normal.en: Believe it or not marks surprise.
normal.cn: believe it or not 用来表示意外。

abstract.en: See a head nodding slowly after an explanation.
abstract.cn: 想象听完解释后慢慢点头。

abstract.en: See two hands shaking on a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在承诺中相握。

abstract.en: See a candle kept burning in doubt.
abstract.cn: 想象疑虑中仍亮着的蜡烛。

examples.en: I believe his story.
examples.cn: 我相信他讲的事。

examples.en: I believe she is still in the office.

dict_mnemonic.text: be 加 lieve（近似 lief，珍爱），把话当成珍爱之物收下就是相信。

root: 古英语 geliefan 由 be- 与 lief（亲爱的）构成，本义「珍视」，中古英语转为「信任」，十七世纪起 believe in 表示信仰。

sensesIntro.en: The same verb covers accepting a fact, holding an opinion and keeping a faith.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词既指接受事实，也指持有看法与怀有信仰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slow nod after hearing an explanation.
core.cn: 核心意象：听完解释后缓缓点头。

intro.en: Believe takes -s, -ed and -ing, and builds belief, -able and -er forms.
intro.cn: believe 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，并构成 belief、-able 与 -er 形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

definition_zh: n. 信徒；信教者；相信某事（或主张某事）的人
definition_en: a person who believes in a religion; a person who is convinced that something is true, right or worthwhile
core_image: 礼拜散场后，门口那位说「信了一辈子」的老人
scene: 礼拜结束后，门口的老人说他一辈子都信。After the service an old man at the door said he had been a believer all his life.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：believer 指宗教上的信徒；句意是礼拜后门口的老人说他一辈子都是信者。

derivatives.zh: 信念；信仰
相信；信任
忠诚的；虔诚的
拥护者；追随者

senses.title: A religious believer
senses.definition: a person who holds a religious faith
senses.definitionCN: 持有宗教信仰的人
senses.example: Believers of several faiths shared the same hall.
senses.exampleCN: 几种信仰的信徒共用同一个礼堂。
senses.why: The agent ending -er on believe first named people who held a faith, which remains its main use.
senses.whyCN: believe 上的施事后缀 -er 最初就指持守信仰的人，这仍是其主用法。

senses.title: Someone convinced of an idea
senses.definition: a person who is convinced that a practice, policy or idea is right or useful
senses.definitionCN: 确信某种做法、政策或想法正确或有益的人
senses.example: She is a believer in long walks and early nights.
senses.exampleCN: 她笃信长距离散步和早睡。
senses.why: Once religion is no longer required, the same word covers any conviction held with confidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不再限于宗教，同一个词就能覆盖任何坚定的确信。

intro.en: Believer is believe plus -er, and believe began with love: to hold something dear was to hold it true.
intro.cn: believer 是 believe 加 -er，而 believe 起初与「爱」有关：珍视某物，就是认为它为真。

items.en: The root leubh meant to love or to hold dear, the deep base of believe.
items.cn: 词根 leubh 意为爱、珍视，是 believe 的深层基础。

items.en: Old English geliefan means to hold something dear and therefore true.
items.cn: 古英语 geliefan 意为「珍视因而信以为真」。

items.en: The prefix be- joins the verb, giving belyfan, to believe.
items.cn: 前缀 be- 加入该动词，形成 belyfan「相信」。

items.en: Middle English believe settles the spelling and the sense of holding as true.
items.cn: 中古英语 believe 固定了拼写与「信以为真」之义。

items.en: The agent ending -er names the person who believes, first in religion.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -er 造出 believer，最初用于宗教。

items.en: The word widens to anyone who supports an idea, as a believer in reform.
items.cn: 词义扩指任何拥护某种主张的人，如 a believer in reform。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps believe and belief beside the longer -er words; the near-meaning group ranks followers from a formal adherent to a new convert.
note.cn: 形近组把 believe 与 belief 放在较长的 -er 词旁边；近义组把追随者从正式的拥护者排到新皈依者。

entries.definition: A feeling that something is true.
A person who takes over a duty.
A dog trained to fetch shot game.

A pupil who follows a teacher teaching.
A person strongly devoted to something.
A person who has adopted a new faith.
entries.definitionCN: 新近改信某种信仰的人。

normalIntro.en: Believer is believe plus the person ending -er. And believe began as to hold dear, which is why faith and love share a root.
normalIntro.cn: believer 是 believe 加表「人」的 -er。而 believe 本义是「珍视」，所以信仰与爱同根。

normal.en: Believe is the verb; believer is the person.
normal.cn: believe 是动词，believer 是那个人。

normal.en: Belief is the state; be careful not to swap them.
normal.cn: belief 是状态，注意别与 believer 混用。

normal.en: A believer in progress trusts that things improve.
normal.cn: a believer in progress 相信事情会变好。

normal.en: Believers is the plural, one l and two e.
normal.cn: 复数是 believers，一个 l 两个 e。

normal.en: To hold something dear is to hold it true.
normal.cn: 珍视某物，就是认为它为真。

abstract.en: A person who lets a claim live rent-free.
abstract.cn: 让某个说法免费住进脑子里的人。

abstract.en: Trust given before evidence arrives.
abstract.cn: 证据到来之前就先给出的信任。

abstract.en: Love wearing the clothes of certainty.
abstract.cn: 穿上「确定」外衣的爱。

examples.en: The chapel holds believers of three different faiths.
examples.cn: 这座礼拜堂容纳三种不同信仰的信徒。

examples.en: He is a believer in plain speaking.
examples.cn: 他笃信有话直说。

examples.en: Believers and sceptics filled the hall alike.
examples.cn: 信者与怀疑者同样挤满了大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：believe「相信」+ -er「人」= believer 信徒。同族辨析：believe 动词、belief 信念、believer 人。记一条古义线索：believe 原义「珍视」，所以「信」里带着「爱」。

root: believe 出自古英语 belyfan「信奉」，由 be- 加 geliefan 构成，深层为原始印欧语 leubh「爱、珍视」——「珍视故以为真」。13 世纪加施事后缀 -er 造出 believer，最初专指宗教信徒，18 世纪扩指任何赞同某种主张的人。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses, one root act: to hold something true because you hold it dear, first in religion and then in any conviction.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项，同一个根本动作：因为珍视所以认定为真——先在宗教里，再扩到任何确信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man at the chapel door saying he has believed all his life
core.cn: 核心意象：礼拜堂门口的老人说他信了一辈子

branches.en: A hand on a worn prayer book.

intro.en: Believer is believe plus the agent ending -er; the Latin layer arrives through the near-synonyms for followers.
intro.cn: believer 是 believe 加施事后缀 -er；拉丁语层次经由「追随者」类近义词进来。

latinIntro.en: Latin credere means to believe or entrust, fides means faith, and devotus means devoted; they give credit, fidelity and devotee.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 credere 意为相信、托付，fides 意为信义，devotus 意为虔诚；它们给出 credit、fidelity 与 devotee。

definition_zh: 好战的；好斗的；尚武的；咄咄逼人的
definition_en: eager to fight or quarrel; showing an aggressive and warlike spirit
core_image: 一只攥紧拳头、浑身炸毛、随时要扑上去的斗鸡
scene: 谈判还没开始，他已经拍着桌子、卷起袖子。His bellicose tone made the negotiation harder before it began.
sceneCN: 这里 bellicose 是「好斗的、咄咄逼人的」（第 1 个义项：性情或言辞好战）；句意是他好斗的腔调让谈判一开始就变得艰难。

pos.zh: 好战的；好斗的；气势汹汹的

collocations.zh: 一肚子火气、想吵架的样子

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「好战性；挑衅态度」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「好斗地」
同根近义词，义为「交战的；好斗的」

senses.title: Eager to fight or quarrel
senses.definition: having or showing a strong desire to fight, argue, or threaten
senses.definitionCN: 一心想打架、争吵或威胁的样子
senses.example: His bellicose tone made the negotiation harder before it began.
senses.exampleCN: 他好斗的腔调让谈判还没开始就变得艰难。
senses.why: The Latin bellum means war, and the suffix -ose means full of.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 bellum 意为「战争」，后缀 -ose 表示「充满」，合起来即「充满战争气」。

senses.title: Warlike in manner of speech or policy
senses.definition: describing talk, writing, or policy that threatens or invites war
senses.definitionCN: 形容言谈、文章或政策带有威胁、挑动战争的味道
senses.example: The editorial criticized the government's bellicose rhetoric.
senses.exampleCN: 社论批评了政府挑衅性的言辞。
senses.why: The war image transfers from fists to words and policies.
senses.whyCN: 「战争」意象从拳脚转移到言语与政策层面。

intro.en: Bellicose comes from Latin bellum, war, plus the suffix -osus.
intro.cn: bellicose 来自拉丁语 bellum「战争」加后缀 -osus「充满」。

items.en: the root delhw- meant to aim at, to urge on.
items.cn: 一般认为词根与「瞄准、驱使」有关（重构形式）。

items.en: bellum meant war; bellicosus meant warlike, eager to fight.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bellum 意为「战争」，bellicosus 意为「好战的」。

items.en: belliqueux carried the same warlike sense into French.
items.cn: 中古法语 belliqueux 沿用好战之义。

items.en: bellicose was borrowed in the fifteenth century for warlike people and nations.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 bellicose，形容好战之人、好战之国。

items.en: today it often describes aggressive speech rather than real warfare.
items.cn: 如今多形容咄咄逼人的言辞，而非真实的战争。

definition_zh: 好斗的；挑衅的；交战的；（n.）交战国；交战方
definition_en: hostile and aggressive, or engaged in war; as a noun, a nation or party waging war
core_image: 额头顶到对方胸口、下巴扬起、眼里带火的挑衅者
scene: 他把胸膛抵到对方身前，声音一句比一句冲。The belligerent driver refused to back down after the small crash.
sceneCN: 这里 belligerent 是「挑衅的、寸步不让的」（第 2 个义项：态度好斗）；句意是小碰擦之后，那个态度挑衅的司机寸步不让。

pos.zh: 好斗的；挑衅的；交战中的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「好斗；交战状态」

senses.title: Engaged in war
senses.definition: taking part in a war or officially recognized as waging war

senses.example: The treaty forced the belligerent powers to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 条约把交战各方逼到了谈判桌前。

senses.title: Hostile and aggressive in manner
senses.definition: behaving in an angry, combative way, ready to argue or fight
senses.definitionCN: 言行带着怒气与火药味，动辄要吵要打
senses.example: The belligerent driver refused to back down after the small crash.
senses.exampleCN: 小碰擦之后，那个态度挑衅的司机寸步不让。
senses.why: The image of waging war shrinks to a personal quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 「进行战争」的画面缩小为个人争吵。

senses.title: A nation or party waging war
senses.definition: a country or group actually fighting a war
senses.definitionCN: 实际参与战争的国家或团体
senses.example: Both belligerents signed the ceasefire at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 交战双方在黎明签署了停火协议。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the war-wager itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词，直接指「进行战争的一方」。

intro.en: Belligerent is Latin bellum, war, plus gerere, to wage or carry on.
intro.cn: belligerent 由拉丁语 bellum「战争」加 gerere「进行」构成。

items.en: the root behind bellum is generally linked to urging and aiming.
items.cn: bellum 的词根一般认为与「驱使、瞄准」有关（重构形式）。

items.en: belligerare meant to wage war, from bellum plus gerere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 belligerare 意为「进行战争」。

items.en: belligerans was the participle meaning waging war.
items.cn: belligerans 是其分词形式，意为「进行战争的」。

items.en: modern political use grew from Spanish belligerante in disputes over recognizing rebel states.
items.cn: 现代政治用法与十九世纪西班牙语 belligerante 有关，用于讨论是否承认叛乱政权为交战方。

items.en: belligerent now covers both the legal warring sense and everyday hostile manners.
items.cn: 如今 belligerent 兼指法律上的交战与日常的好斗态度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bell- war root or spelling; the near-meaning group gathers hostile manners.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bell-「战争」词根或拼写；近义组汇集敌对态度词。

entries.definitionCN: 好战的——同根近亲，侧重性情
反叛的——同含 bellum 词根

normalIntro.en: Belligerent is bellum plus gerere: waging war.
normalIntro.cn: belligerent 是 bellum 加 gerere：进行战争。

normal.en: The noun belligerents means warring sides.
normal.cn: 名词 belligerents 指交战各方。

normal.en: The noun form of the manner is belligerence.
normal.cn: 态度义的名词形式是 belligerence。

normal.en: It shares bell- with rebellion.
normal.cn: 它与 rebellion 同含 bell- 词根。

normal.en: A belligerent tone starts fights.
normal.cn: 挑衅的语气挑起争斗。

normal.en: Compare with bellicose and hostile.
normal.cn: 对比 bellicose 与 hostile。

abstract.en: See a chest pushed forward and a chin raised.
abstract.cn: 看挺起的胸膛和扬起的下巴。

abstract.en: Feel sparks before the quarrel flares.
abstract.cn: 感受争吵爆发前的火花。

abstract.en: Picture two flags facing each other across a field.
abstract.cn: 想象战场上对峙的两面旗帜。

examples.en: The belligerent driver refused to back down after the small crash.
examples.cn: 小碰擦之后，那个态度挑衅的司机寸步不让。

examples.en: The treaty forced the belligerent powers to the table.
examples.cn: 条约把交战各方逼到了谈判桌前。

examples.en: Both belligerents signed the ceasefire at dawn.
examples.cn: 交战双方在黎明签署了停火协议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「玻璃舰」——开着玻璃舰横冲直撞，见谁撞谁，好斗成性。

root: 拉丁语 bellum「战争」加 gerere「进行、从事」，派生动词 belligerare「进行战争」，分词 belligerans 进入现代拉丁语后借入英语；现代政治义与十九世纪西班牙语 belligerante 的使用有关。同根词有 bellicose、rebellion、rebel 等。

sensesIntro.en: One word wages war between nations, then brings the same fire into personal quarrels.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个词，先在国家之间开战，再把同一股火气带进个人争吵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest pushed forward, a chin raised, eyes on fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：挺胸抬头、眼里带火的挑衅者。

intro.en: Belligerent pairs the war root bell- with the verb gerere.
intro.cn: belligerent 把「战争」词根 bell- 与动词 gerere 配对。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair bellum and gerere heads this word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bellum 与 gerere 的组合统领这个词族。

latinEntries.meaning: to wage war; direct source of belligerent
latinEntries.meaningCN: 进行战争；belligerent 的直接来源

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「好斗」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「好斗地」

definition_zh: 腰带；地带；传送带
definition_en: a strip worn around the waist, or a long narrow area
core_image: 工人系紧皮带走进车间
scene: 他系紧皮带，把工具包挂上去。He tightened his belt before climbing.
sceneCN: 这里 belt 是「腰带」（第 1 个义项：系在腰上的带状物）；句意是他爬之前系紧了腰带。

pos.zh: 动词：用带子系住；（口语）猛击

derivatives.zh: 由 belt 加 -ed 构成，义为「系腰带的」
由 belt 加 -ing 构成，义为「传动带材料」
由 belt 与 way 复合，义为「环城公路」

senses.title: A strip around the waist
senses.definition: a strip of leather or cloth worn around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 系在腰上的皮革或布带
senses.example: He tightened his belt before climbing.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬之前系紧了腰带。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, borrowed from Latin for a strap.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，借自拉丁语中表示带子的词。

senses.title: A long narrow area
senses.definition: a long region with a special feature
senses.definitionCN: 具有某种特征的长条区域
senses.example: This city sits in the industrial belt.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市位于工业地带。
senses.why: A belt wraps around, so a wide band of land took the name.
senses.whyCN: 腰带是环绕的，因此一大片带状土地也得此名。

senses.title: A moving strip in a machine
senses.definition: a continuous strip that carries things
senses.definitionCN: 连续运转、用来运送物品的带子
senses.example: The boxes moved along the belt.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子沿着传送带移动。
senses.why: The shape of a waist belt matches the loop inside machines.
senses.whyCN: 腰带的形状与机器里的环形带一致。

intro.en: Belt came into Old English from Latin balteus, a strap.
intro.cn: belt 经拉丁语 balteus（带子）进入古英语。

items.en: balteus meant a girdle or strap.
items.cn: balteus 意为「腰带、带子」。

items.en: belt named a waist strap.
items.cn: belt 指腰间的带子。

items.en: belts held tools and swords.
items.cn: 腰带用来挂工具和剑。

items.en: machines gained moving belts.
items.cn: 机器开始使用运转的带子。

items.en: belt also names long regions of land.
items.cn: 如今 belt 也指狭长的地带。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gives strap and zone words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是带子与区域的词。

entries.definition: a cloth band worn round the waist
an area with a special purpose

normalIntro.en: A belt is a strip that holds things together or marks a band of land.
normalIntro.cn: belt 是能把东西束住的带子，也能指一条带状土地。

normal.en: The plural is belts.
normal.cn: 复数是 belts。

normal.en: A seat belt keeps you safe in a car.
normal.cn: seat belt 让你在车里更安全。

normal.en: Tighten the belt also means spend less.
normal.cn: tighten the belt 也指节省开支。

normal.en: An industrial belt is a factory region.
normal.cn: industrial belt 指工业地带。

normal.en: The verb means to fasten with a belt.
normal.cn: 动词义指用带子系住。

abstract.en: See a worker pulling a leather belt tight.
abstract.cn: 想象工人把皮带勒紧。

abstract.en: See factories lined along a wide road.
abstract.cn: 想象沿大路排开的工厂。

abstract.en: See boxes rolling on a moving strip.
abstract.cn: 想象箱子在运转的带上移动。

examples.en: He tightened his belt before climbing.
examples.cn: 他爬之前系紧了腰带。

examples.en: This city sits in the industrial belt.
examples.cn: 这座城市位于工业地带。

examples.en: The boxes moved along the belt.
examples.cn: 箱子沿着传送带移动。

dict_mnemonic.text: belt 读起来短而紧，正像一条勒紧的腰带。

root: 借自拉丁语 balteus（腰带），古英语作 belt，本指腰间带子，十九世纪起用于机器传动带，并引申指带状地域。

sensesIntro.en: The same strip wraps a waist, a machine and a stretch of land.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一条「带」束住腰、绕住机器，也圈出一片土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worker pulling a leather belt tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：工人勒紧皮带。

intro.en: Belt takes -s, -ed and -ing, and joins way to form beltway.
intro.cn: belt 可加 -s、-ed、-ing，还能与 way 复合成 beltway。

latinIntro.en: The source is Latin balteus, a girdle.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁语 balteus，意为腰带。

definition_zh: 弯曲；弯道；屈服
definition_en: to make something curved, or a curve in a road
core_image: 柳枝被风压弯又弹回
scene: 风把河边的柳枝压了下去。The wind bent the willow branches.
sceneCN: 这里 bend 是「使弯曲」（第 1 个义项：把直的东西压成弧形）；句意是风把柳枝吹弯了。

derivatives.zh: 由 bend 加 -er 构成，义为「弯曲者、狂欢」
由 bend 加 -y 构成，义为「易弯曲的」
由 un- 加 bend 构成，义为「弄直、放松」
由 bend 的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「弯的」

senses.title: To make something curved
senses.definition: to force something straight into a curve
senses.definitionCN: 把直的东西压成弧形
senses.example: The wind bent the willow branches.
senses.exampleCN: 风把柳枝吹弯了。
senses.why: This is the core sense, and it works for metal, wood and limbs.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，适用于金属、木头和肢体。

senses.title: A curve in a road
senses.definition: a place where a road turns
senses.definitionCN: 道路转弯的地方
senses.example: Slow down before the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 拐弯前要减速。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, naming the curved part itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，用来指弯曲的那一段。

senses.title: To give in
senses.definition: to yield to pressure or rules
senses.definitionCN: 在压力或规则前让步
senses.example: He refused to bend to their demands.
senses.exampleCN: 他拒绝向他们的要求屈服。
senses.why: Something that bends under force gives up its straight shape.
senses.whyCN: 在力量下弯曲的东西，放弃了原本笔直的形状。

intro.en: Bend first meant to bend a bow, from an old Germanic verb.
intro.cn: bend 最初指把弓拉弯，来自古老的日耳曼语动词。

items.en: bendan meant to bend a bow.
items.cn: bendan 意为「把弓拉弯」。

items.en: the verb spread to any bending.
items.cn: 这个动词扩展到任何弯曲动作。

items.en: the noun named a curve in a road.
items.cn: 名词开始指道路的弯道。

items.en: bend also meant to submit.
items.cn: bend 也开始表示「屈服」。

items.en: bent is both past tense and adjective.
items.cn: 如今 bent 既是过去式，也是形容词。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives curve words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示弯曲的词。

normalIntro.en: Bend means to force a straight thing into a curve.
normalIntro.cn: bend 就是把直的东西逼成弧形。

normal.en: The past tense is bent.
normal.cn: 过去式是 bent。

normal.en: Bend down means lower your body.
normal.cn: bend down 指弯下身体。

normal.en: Bend the rules means loosen them a little.
normal.cn: bend the rules 指对规则稍作变通。

normal.en: A bend in the road is a curve.
normal.cn: a bend in the road 就是路的弯道。

normal.en: Bend to pressure means give in.
normal.cn: bend to pressure 指在压力下屈服。

abstract.en: See a willow branch pressed low by wind.
abstract.cn: 想象柳枝被风吹得低垂。

abstract.en: See a road curving around a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象道路绕山转弯。

abstract.en: See a metal bar folded by hands.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把金属条折弯。

examples.en: The wind bent the willow branches.
examples.cn: 风把柳枝吹弯了。

examples.en: Slow down before the bend.
examples.cn: 拐弯前要减速。

examples.en: He refused to bend to their demands.
examples.cn: 他拒绝向他们的要求屈服。

dict_mnemonic.text: bend 的 b 像弓身，把 d 压弯就成了弧形。

root: 古英语 bendan 本指给弓上弦、使弓弯曲，中古英语扩展为一切弯曲动作，十六世纪起作名词指弯道，十七世纪引申为屈服。

sensesIntro.en: A curved branch, a curved road and a yielding will all use bend.
sensesIntro.cn: 弯下的枝条、弯曲的道路、屈服的心志，都用 bend。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a willow branch pressed low by wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：被风吹得低垂的柳枝。

intro.en: Bend takes -s, -ing and the irregular past bent.
intro.cn: bend 可加 -s、-ing，过去式是不规则的 bent。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 在……下面；有失（身份）
definition_en: in or to a lower position than something, or below the level of
core_image: 树根在泥土下悄悄伸展
scene: 树根在泥土下面悄悄伸展开。Roots spread beneath the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 beneath 是「在……下面」（第 1 个义项：处在某物覆盖之下的较低位置）；句意是树根在泥土下蔓延。

derivatives.zh: 与 beneath 同源的介词，义为「在……底下」
与 beneath 同源的形容词，义为「下面的」

senses.title: Under something
senses.definition: in a lower position, often covered by something
senses.definitionCN: 处在较低位置，常被某物覆盖
senses.example: Roots spread beneath the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 树根在泥土下蔓延。
senses.why: This is the literal sense, close to under but more literary.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面义，接近 under，但更带书面色彩。

senses.title: Below one's dignity
senses.definition: too low or unworthy for someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人来说太低微、不值得
senses.example: He thinks such work is beneath him.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得这种活有失他的身份。
senses.why: Low place in space turned into low rank in social terms.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的低位置，转为身份上的低。

intro.en: Beneath is be- plus an old form of neath, meaning low.
intro.cn: beneath 是 be- 加上 neath 的古老形式，意为「低」。

items.en: beneothan meant below.
items.cn: beneothan 意为「在下面」。

items.en: beneath became the usual form.
items.cn: beneath 成为通用形式。

items.en: the word also marked low rank.
items.cn: 这个词也开始标记低微的身份。

items.en: beneath gained a formal, literary tone.
items.cn: beneath 带上正式与文学的色彩。

items.en: beneath is rarer than under in speech.
items.cn: 如今口语中 beneath 比 under 少见。

note.en: The look-alike group rhymes in -eath; the near-meaning group gives other under words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -eath 收尾；近义组是其他表示下方的词。

normalIntro.en: Beneath is the literary cousin of under.
normalIntro.cn: beneath 是 under 的书面近亲。

normal.en: Beneath is more formal than under.
normal.cn: beneath 比 under 更正式。

normal.en: Beneath the surface means hidden.
normal.cn: beneath the surface 指藏在表面之下。

normal.en: Beneath someone can mean unworthy of them.
normal.cn: beneath someone 可以指有失其身份。

normal.en: The word ends like breath and wreath.
normal.cn: 这个词与 breath、wreath 押韵。

normal.en: The spelling keeps be- at the front.
normal.cn: 拼写开头保留 be-。

abstract.en: See roots sliding under dark soil.
abstract.cn: 想象树根在暗色泥土下伸展。

abstract.en: See a fish passing under a boat.
abstract.cn: 想象一条鱼从船下游过。

abstract.en: See a proud face turning from small work.
abstract.cn: 想象骄傲的脸避开琐碎的活。

examples.en: Roots spread beneath the soil.
examples.cn: 树根在泥土下蔓延。

examples.en: He thinks such work is beneath him.
examples.cn: 他觉得这种活有失他的身份。

examples.en: A small stream runs beneath the bridge.
examples.cn: 一条小溪从桥下流过。

dict_mnemonic.text: be 加 neath（低），处在低处，就是 beneath。

root: 古英语 beneothan 由 be- 与 neothan（低处）构成，本义「在下方」，十六世纪起引申指身份低微，现代多用于书面语。

sensesIntro.en: A lower place in space and a lower place in rank both sit beneath.
sensesIntro.cn: 空间上的低处与身份上的低位，都落在 beneath 之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: roots sliding under dark soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：树根在暗色泥土下伸展。

intro.en: Beneath is a fixed form that shares its root with underneath.
intro.cn: beneath 形式固定，与 underneath 同根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自古英语。

definition_zh: 恩人；捐助人；资助人；行善者
definition_en: a person who gives money or other help to a person, cause, or organization
core_image: 在捐赠名单顶端签下名字、把钱袋递给学校的人
scene: 新图书馆落成那天，人们把最大的感谢献给他。The library's marble wall lists the name of its chief benefactor.
sceneCN: 这里 benefactor 是「捐助人、恩人」（第 1 个义项：出资出力的行善者）；句意是图书馆的大理石墙上刻着主要捐助人的名字。

derivatives.zh: 由同根动词性成分加名词后缀构成，义为「善行；捐款」
阴性形式，义为「女恩人；女捐助人」
同根关联词，义为「受益人」

senses.title: A person who gives money or help
senses.definition: someone who supports a person, school, hospital, or cause with money or aid
senses.definitionCN: 以钱财或帮助支持个人、学校、医院或事业的人
senses.example: The library's marble wall lists the name of its chief benefactor.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的大理石墙上刻着主要捐助人的名字。
senses.why: Bene means good and factor means a doer, so the word names a doer of good.
senses.whyCN: bene 意为「好」，factor 意为「做事的人」，合起来即「行善之人」。

senses.title: A protector or patron in a broader sense
senses.definition: anyone who looks after or promotes another's welfare, not only with money
senses.definitionCN: 广义上护佑、提携他人的人，不限于出资
senses.example: The professor was a quiet benefactor to generations of young scholars.
senses.exampleCN: 这位教授是几代年轻学者默默的扶助者。
senses.why: Doing good can mean opening doors, not only opening a purse.
senses.whyCN: 「行善」不只是掏钱，也可以是为人开门引路。

intro.en: Benefactor is Latin bene, well, plus factor, a doer.
intro.cn: benefactor 由拉丁语 bene「好」加 factor「做事者」构成。

items.en: the root dhe- meant to set, to do.
items.cn: 词根 dhe- 意为「放置、做」（重构形式）。

items.en: benefactor meant a doer of good, from bene plus facere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 benefactor 意为「行善者」，由 bene 加 facere 构成。

items.en: the title was used for kings and patrons in inscriptions.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语铭文中用作君王与赞助人的尊称。

items.en: English adopted benefactor in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语采纳 benefactor 一词。

items.en: it now names donors to schools, museums, and charities.
items.cn: 如今多指向学校、博物馆、慈善机构捐资的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the bene- or fact- roots; the near-meaning group gathers words for givers and supporters.
note.cn: 形近组共享 bene- 或 fact- 词根；近义组汇集给予者、支持者类词。

entries.definitionCN: 善行；捐款——benefactor 的行为名词
作恶者——前缀相反的对照词
有益的——同含 bene- 词根

entries.definition: a regular supporter, especially of the arts

sceneCN: 这里 benevolent 指待人心怀善意、乐于给予（第 1 个义项：善意待人）；句意为这位仁慈的老师课后留下来帮助最弱的学生。

senses.title: Kind and wishing well
senses.definition: kind, generous and wishing good for other people
senses.definitionCN: 善良、慷慨，并希望他人过得好
senses.example: The benevolent teacher stayed after class to help the weakest students.
senses.exampleCN: 这位仁慈的老师课后留下来帮助最弱的学生。
senses.why: The Latin word is built from 'well' and 'to wish': benevolence is literally a good wish directed at someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词由「好」与「愿望」构成：仁慈字面上就是朝向某人的美好祝愿。

senses.title: Power used for others' good
senses.definition: of a ruler or authority, using power for the welfare of those under it
senses.definitionCN: 指统治者或权威把权力用于治下之人的福祉
senses.example: The benevolent ruler lowered taxes during the famine.
senses.exampleCN: 这位宽厚的统治者在饥荒期间减税。
senses.why: Power normally flows downward; when the word is attached to a ruler, it claims the flow is turned to benefit the ruled.
senses.whyCN: 权力通常自上而下流动；当这个词用于统治者时，它声称这股流向被转向了被统治者。

senses.title: Organized charity
senses.definition: of a fund or society, set up to give aid to those in need
senses.definitionCN: 指为帮助有需要者而设立的基金或团体
senses.example: A benevolent fund covered the family's medical costs.
senses.exampleCN: 一项慈善基金承担了这个家庭的医疗费用。
senses.why: The good wish becomes an institution: money is collected and distributed by rule rather than by impulse.
senses.whyCN: 美好的祝愿变成制度：钱按规则收集与分发，而不是凭一时冲动。

senses.title: A kindly expression
senses.definition: of a look or smile, expressing kindly goodwill
senses.definitionCN: 指神情或微笑流露出善意的温和
senses.example: She gave the child a benevolent smile.
senses.exampleCN: 她对孩子露出慈祥的微笑。
senses.why: A face is the smallest place where the wish becomes visible; a slight softening of the eyes reports the inner direction.
senses.whyCN: 脸是愿望变得可见的最小场所；眼神略微放软就报告了内在的朝向。

senses.title: A mutual aid association
senses.definition: a society formed so that members help one another in difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 为成员在困难时互相帮助而组成的团体
senses.example: The miners' benevolent society paid for funerals.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工的互助会承担丧葬费用。
senses.why: When people cannot rely on the state, they pool risk among themselves, and the good wish becomes a contract of mutual help.
senses.whyCN: 当人们无法依赖国家时，就在彼此之间分摊风险，美好的祝愿变成了互助的契约。

senses.title: A kindly reading of others
senses.definition: in psychology, the tendency to interpret others' actions as well meant
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，倾向于把他人的行为解释为出于好意
senses.example: A benevolent attribution reduces conflict in a team.
senses.exampleCN: 善意的归因能减少团队中的冲突。
senses.why: Interpretation is a choice between suspicion and goodwill; the word names the choice that assumes the better motive.
senses.whyCN: 解读是在猜疑与善意之间的选择；这个词命名那个假定较好动机的选择。

senses.title: A god disposed to good
senses.definition: in theology, of a deity, disposed toward human welfare
senses.definitionCN: 在神学中，指神对人类福祉怀有善意
senses.example: The hymn praises a benevolent creator.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗称颂慈悲的造物主。
senses.why: The same wish is projected onto the largest power imaginable, and the universe is described as friendly rather than indifferent.
senses.whyCN: 同样的愿望被投射到可想象的最大力量上，宇宙于是被描述为友善而非冷漠。

senses.title: An authoritarian with good intentions
senses.definition: in politics, an absolute ruler who claims to act for the subjects' welfare
senses.definitionCN: 在政治学中，指声称替被统治者谋福利的绝对统治者
senses.example: The essay examines the limits of benevolent dictatorship.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章探讨开明专制的局限。
senses.why: Good intentions do not change where the decision sits: the word can describe kindness without granting the ruled any say.
senses.whyCN: 善意并不改变决定所在的位置：这个词可以描述仁慈，却不给被统治者任何发言权。

intro.en: Benevolent is a Latin compound meaning 'wishing well', built from bene and velle.

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the 15c. from Latin, first for generous patrons and later for kindly feeling in general.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪从拉丁语借入这个形容词，最初指慷慨的资助者，后来泛指善意的情感。

items.en: The Latin phrase bene velle meant 'to wish well', and the adjective benevolens named one who wishes well.
items.cn: 拉丁短语 bene velle 意为「祝愿良好」，形容词 benevolens 命名祝愿良好的人。

items.en: Bene 'well' is the adverb of bonus 'good', and appears in benefit, benediction and benefactor.
items.cn: bene「好地」是 bonus「好」的副词形式，出现于 benefit、benediction 与 benefactor 中。

items.en: Velle 'to wish, to be willing' gives voluntary and volunteer, so the wish and the willingness share one root.
items.cn: velle「愿望、愿意」产生 voluntary 与 volunteer，因此愿望与意愿共享一个词根。

items.en: The word moved from personal feeling to institutions: benevolent funds and societies made the good wish into an organized practice.
items.cn: 这个词从个人情感转向制度：慈善基金与互助会把美好的愿望变成有组织的实践。

sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：bequest 指遗嘱所留的财物；句意是遗嘱把那栋老屋作为遗赠留给乡村学校。

senses.title: The act of leaving by will
senses.definition: the act of giving property to someone through a will
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗嘱把财产给予某人的行为
senses.example: The bequest took effect only after probate.
senses.exampleCN: 遗赠须待遗嘱认证后才生效。
senses.why: The word grew from a verb meaning to say something in a will, so the act came before the thing.
senses.whyCN: 该词从「在遗嘱中说出」的动词长出，因此「行为」先于「财物」。

senses.title: The property left
senses.definition: the money or property given to someone by a will
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗嘱给予某人的钱财或房产
senses.example: Her bequest paid for the new reading room.
senses.exampleCN: 她的遗赠出资修建了新的阅览室。
senses.why: English lets the noun name both the giving and what is given, a very common double duty.
senses.whyCN: 英语让这个名词同时指「给予」与「所给之物」，这是极常见的双重职责。

senses.title: Anything handed down
senses.definition: something passed on to later people, such as an idea or a tradition
senses.definitionCN: 传给后人的东西，如思想或传统
senses.example: The library is a bequest of one generation to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆是一代人对下一代人的馈赠。
senses.why: Once the property sense is fixed, any transferred good can be called a bequest in literary use.
senses.whyCN: 一旦财物义固定，任何被移交的好东西都能在书面语中称为 bequest。

intro.en: Bequest comes from an old verb meaning to say something in a will. The saying became the giving, and the giving became the gift.
intro.cn: bequest 出自一个古动词，意为「在遗嘱中说出」。说定成了给予，给予又成了所给之物。

items.en: Old English cwethan means to say, and becwethan means to say something in a will.
items.cn: 古英语 cwethan 意为「说」，becwethan 意为「在遗嘱中说定」。

items.en: Middle English biqueste is the noun of the saying, a will or a legacy.
items.cn: 中古英语 biqueste 是「说定」之事的名称，指遗嘱或遗赠。

items.en: The spelling shifts toward bequest under the influence of bequeath.
items.cn: 受 bequeath 影响，拼写向 bequest 靠拢。

items.en: Law fixes the word on property left by will, both the act and the thing.
items.cn: 法律把该词固定为遗嘱所留财产，兼指行为与财物。

items.en: Writers use the word for anything handed down, such as a bequest of ideas.
items.cn: 文人用该词指任何传承下来的东西，如思想的遗赠。

items.en: The legal sense remains primary, and the figurative sense stays literary.
items.cn: 法律义仍为主，比喻义保持书面色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -quest and -est endings where the spelling goes wrong; the near-meaning group separates the legal instrument from what is actually received.
note.cn: 形近组保留易拼错的 -quest 与 -est 词尾；近义组把法律文书与真正到手的东西分开。

normalIntro.cn: bequest 里藏着 quest，但什么也不必寻找：东西在遗嘱里被说定，然后被给予。

normal.en: A will says it, so a bequest is what was said.

normal.en: A legacy is close, but often means the whole estate.

normal.en: Do not confuse it with request, which only asks.

abstract.cn: 来自一间你再进不去的房间的声音。

abstract.en: Property obeying a sentence.

abstract.en: The dead still deciding where things go.
abstract.cn: 逝者仍在决定东西的去向。

examples.cn: 这座美术馆靠一笔遗赠建立。

examples.en: She made several small bequests to former students.
examples.cn: 她给几位旧日学生留下了小额遗赠。

examples.en: Clean water is the greatest bequest of that generation.
examples.cn: 清洁的水是那一代人最大的馈赠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 一对词辨析：bequeath 是动词「遗赠」，bequest 是名词「遗赠（物）」。记词源画面：在遗嘱里「说定」给谁——说出来的是行为，说定的东西是财物。别与 request「请求」混。

root: 出自古英语 becwethan「在遗嘱中说定」，由 be- 加 cwethan「说」构成；名词中古英语作 biqueste，14 世纪受 bequeath 影响拼作 bequest。16 世纪法律固定为「遗嘱所留财产」，兼指行为与财物；19 世纪扩出「传承之物」的书面义。

senses.title: To deprive of a loved one

intro.cn: beret 是整体借入的词；有用的构件是它的拉丁语祖先 birrus，以及围绕它的法语小词尾。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin birrus means a hooded cloak and Medieval Latin birretum means a cap; caput, head, is the other Latin thread here.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语 birrus 意为带风帽的斗篷，中世纪拉丁语 birretum 意为帽；caput「头」是这里另一条拉丁线索。

definition_zh: 除……之外（还有）；而且
definition_en: in addition to something, or also
core_image: 桌上摆着茶，旁边还多一碟点心
scene: 桌上除了茶，还摆着一碟点心。Besides tea, there were cakes on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 besides 是「除……之外还有」（第 1 个义项：在原有之外另加）；句意是除了茶，桌上还有点心。

derivatives.zh: besides 去掉 s 的形式，义为「在……旁边」
与 besides 同源的副词，义为「到一边」
与 besides 同源的名词，义为「侧面」

senses.title: In addition to
senses.definition: as well as something else
senses.definitionCN: 在原有之外另加
senses.example: Besides tea, there were cakes on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 除了茶，桌上还有点心。
senses.why: This sense adds, not excludes, so the extra thing is included.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项是追加而非排除，所以额外的东西也被包含。

senses.title: Moreover
senses.definition: used to add a further point
senses.definitionCN: 用来补充另一点
senses.example: It is late, and besides, it is raining.
senses.exampleCN: 天晚了，而且还在下雨。
senses.why: Standing beside the first point, the word adds a second.
senses.whyCN: 站在第一个论点旁边，再添上第二个。

intro.en: Besides began as the adverb form of beside.
intro.cn: besides 最初是 beside 的副词形式。

items.en: besides meant by the side.
items.cn: besides 意为「在旁侧」。

items.en: the word began to mean in addition.
items.cn: 这个词开始表示「此外」。

items.en: besides and beside split in use.
items.cn: besides 与 beside 的用法分开。

items.en: the adverb besides grew common.
items.cn: 副词用法变得常见。

items.en: besides adds, while except removes.
items.cn: 如今 besides 表示追加，except 表示排除。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -sides ending; the near-meaning group gives adding words.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -sides 收尾；近义组是表示追加的词。

normalIntro.en: Besides adds something extra to what is already there.
normalIntro.cn: besides 在已有之外再加一样。

normal.en: Besides has an s, beside does not.
normal.cn: besides 有 s，beside 没有。

normal.en: Besides adds, except removes.
normal.cn: besides 是加法，except 是减法。

normal.en: Besides can start a sentence with a comma.
normal.cn: besides 作副词时后面常加逗号。

normal.en: And besides adds a second reason.
normal.cn: and besides 用来补充第二个理由。

normal.en: The word is fixed in form.
normal.cn: 这个词形式固定不变。

abstract.en: See tea on a table with cakes beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上茶旁边还有点心。

abstract.en: See one more line added to a list.
abstract.cn: 想象清单上又添了一行。

abstract.en: See rain falling after a late evening.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜又下起雨来。

examples.en: Besides tea, there were cakes on the table.
examples.cn: 除了茶，桌上还有点心。

examples.en: It is late, and besides, it is raining.
examples.cn: 天晚了，而且还在下雨。

examples.en: Nobody besides you knows the answer.
examples.cn: 除了你，没人知道答案。

dict_mnemonic.text: beside 加一个 s，从「在旁边」变成「再加一样」。

root: 由 beside 加副词性 -s 构成，中古英语指「在旁侧」，十四世纪起转为「此外、而且」，与表示排除的 except 形成对照。

sensesIntro.en: One form adds a thing and adds a point, never removes.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既加东西也加论点，从不排除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tea on a table with cakes beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上茶旁还有点心。

intro.en: Besides is fixed, but its side root still builds beside and aside.
intro.cn: besides 形式固定，其 side 词根仍可构成 beside 与 aside。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word is Middle English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，这个词来自中古英语。
